preamble: Backing and occlusion of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] to the voiced uvular stop [ɢ]. In central and northwestern Iranian Persian, including the Tehrani standard, the letter غ, which stood for [ɣ] in Early New Persian and Classical Persian, merged with ق into a single phoneme whose usual realization is a voiced uvular stop [ɢ], with fricative [ɣ ~ ʁ] only in unstressed intervocalic position. The eastern varieties, Dari and Tajik, preserve the fricative.

examples.from: Classical Persian ġam /ˈɣam/ 'grief, sorrow' (Dari [ɣäm], Tajik ғам [ʁäm])
examples.note: Wiktionary transcribes the Iranian form phonemically as [qæm]; the merged ق/غ phoneme is realized as voiced uvular [ɢ] word-initially.
In modern Tehrani Persian there is little to no difference in the pronunciation of غ and ق.
Wiktionary again writes the Iranian form phonemically as [qæɹb̥]; the merged phoneme is a voiced uvular stop in initial position.

sources: Reza Asa, M. (2016). An Acoustic Study of the Manner of Articulation of Uvular Consonant /G/ in Standard Persian. ʿIlm-i Zabān 4(6), 101–130. https://doaj.org/article/01f15dee99da4420928bd67be90c2fea
